channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Hundreds of people gather for 'Belgium's longest lunch table' at Meise Botanic Garden
item.description: It is an attempt to break the record for Belgium’s longest lunch table and draw attention to child poverty.

item.title: Fire scorches multi-studio apartment building in Ixelles
item.description: The fire started at about 11:45 in a studio on the third floor of the four-storey building.

item.title: One person seriously injured in stabbing in Anderlecht overnight
item.description: Initial findings suggest the victim was attacked in the street by one person. The motive for the assault is not yet known.

item.title: Weekend heritage days in Brussels see over 270 events in their program
item.description: The weekend programme includes guided tours, walks, cycle rides, exhibitions, lectures, performances and special openings.

item.title: More than 270 ways to discover Brussels differently this weekend with Heritage Days
item.description: The 38th edition of the Heritage Days takes place on Saturday 19 and Sunday 20 September, with more than 270 activities across the capital’s 19 municipalities.

item.title: Brussels taxi industry protests 'Ten years of being stifled by multinationals'
item.description: Protesters say that a decade of political inaction and competition from multinationals such as Uber is squeezing their livelihoods.

item.title: Crackdown on LGBTQ+ people in Turkey has troubling link to Brussels
item.description: A fierce crackdown on LGBTQ+ people in Turkey has led to raids and arrests, and the fallout is now even reaching Brussels, where people will take to the streets in protest.

item.title: King Baudouin Foundation invests over €1 million for cycling infrastructure projects in Brussels
item.description: For this second edition, an independent jury selected six projects completed in 2024 or 2025.

item.title: Museum dedicated to iconic Le Chat comic character may not open in Ixelles after all
item.description: According to several media reports, 72-year-old cartoonist Geluck, has contacted the Brussels government to withdraw from the project

item.title: Brussels goes car-free on Sunday: Everything you need to know
item.description: Brussels will go car-free on Sunday, with free public transport, activities across the capital and special events marking 50 years of the Brussels Metro. Here's everything you need to know.

item.title: Some Brussels neighbourhoods might soon lose second weekly white-bag rubbish collection
item.description: Brussels will redraw its rubbish collection map based on population density and housing type, while two neighbourhoods prepare to test collective bins.

item.title: Combatting excessive rents: Constitutional Court upholds framework to protect Brussels tenants
item.description: "The Court’s ruling does not mean that the work is done. On the contrary. It is now our task to make this policy as efficient as possible."

item.title: 'Our house is on fire': Greenpeace stages protest at the federal parliament
item.description: Greenpeace staged a protest outside the federal parliament in Brussels on Thursday as the new parliamentary session began.

item.title: Who would Belgians choose if they could directly elect their Prime Minister?
item.description: A new poll reveals who Belgians would choose to lead the country if they could directly elect their Prime Minister, with striking differences between Flanders, Brussels and Wallonia.

item.title: Drive baby drive: How Brussels traffic drives everyone mad
item.description: "You have the cars, which have been here for generations, taking up all the space they need. And then you have the invasive species – the bikes, scooters, joggers and pedestrians – all trying to grab a share of the space."

item.title: Brussels' debt could become three times as large as its revenue in five years
item.description: How broke are the regions and communities in Belgium? And how easily could they dig themselves out of a financial hole in the future?

item.title: Man held two teenage boys as 'real slaves' in Brussels flat as their father lay dying
item.description: A 25-year-old man accused of violence against teenagers, neighbours and former partners allegedly terrorised residents of a Molenbeek building for nearly two years.

item.title: Students protest in Brussels against an increase in tuition fees
item.description: Hundreds of students from French-speaking higher education institutions marched through central Brussels on Wednesday to protest against the rising cost of student life

item.title: Far-right MP freed after being stuck in Flemish Parliament toilet for 13 hours
item.description: Vlaams Belang MP Frédéric Erens was freed by emergency services after a defective lock left him trapped in a toilet at the Flemish Parliament for nearly 13 hours.

item.title: Major traffic disruptions expected in Brussels as student protest against reforms on Wednesday
item.description: Police are warning of major traffic disruption in and around Brussels' city centre.
